nodes.label: Tool Approval System
nodes.rationale: Interactive approval gives users full control over dangerous AI tool actions (file writes, shell commands). Dangerous capabilities (WriteFiles, ExecuteShell, SystemModification) always require approval by default; safe tools like read_file skip approval. Checks occur at three levels: tool, agent service, and user.

nodes.label: Approval Callback (async callback pattern)
nodes.rationale: Async callback lets the agent service wait non-blockingly for the user's decision via async/await, staying compatible with streaming responses while decoupling the agent from the TUI.

nodes.label: Channel-Based Communication
nodes.rationale: Each approval request carries its own mpsc response channel, giving a clean async/await flow with no shared mutable state between the agent service and the TUI.

nodes.label: Capability-Based Permissions
nodes.rationale: Tools declare capabilities; dangerous capabilities automatically require approval. Chosen for extensibility so future tool types inherit correct security behavior without per-tool policy code.

nodes.label: Modal Approval Dialog
nodes.rationale: Full-screen modal prevents any other interaction, forcing focus on the security decision; two-view mode (simple vs detailed JSON) balances quick decisions against thorough review.

nodes.label: Auto-Approve Mode
nodes.rationale: Bypass mechanism kept only for trusted/testing scenarios (--auto-approve flag or with_auto_approve_tools); explicitly flagged as dangerous and not recommended for normal use.

nodes.label: Agent Service Integration (approval)
nodes.rationale: Three design options were weighed for getting approval decisions into the agent service: (A) pass event sender into AgentService, (B) callback function, (C) keep it in the TUI layer via ApprovalRequired errors and retry. Option B (approval callback) was recommended and ultimately implemented because the agent service lacks access to the TUI event sender.

nodes.label: Windows MSVC dlltool Build Issue
nodes.rationale: cargo clippy could not run because the Windows MSVC toolchain lacked MinGW tools (dlltool.exe not found); explicitly assessed as an environment setup issue, not a code quality problem.

nodes.label: Multi-Provider Support
nodes.rationale: Rated critical because users expect multi-provider support as advertised — config supports 6+ providers but only Anthropic worked, making it a production blocker for 1.0.

nodes.label: Error Recovery & Resilience
nodes.rationale: Rated critical because the implementation could crash or hang on network issues; production apps need retry with exponential backoff, timeouts, rate-limit handling, and crash recovery.

nodes.label: Security Hardening
nodes.rationale: Rated critical because handling user code and API keys requires robust security — keys were stored in plaintext; plan includes OS keyring storage, path validation, bash sanitization, tool blacklist, and audit log.

nodes.label: Enhanced Tool System
nodes.rationale: Only 3 tools (read, write, bash) existed — too limited for real coding workflows; plan adds List, Search, Git, WebFetch, Editor, Diff, Test, and Lint tools.

nodes.label: Approval System v2 Enhancements
nodes.rationale: v1 approval is functional but limited; v2 adds session memory, whitelists, diff preview, approval history, bulk approve, pattern matching, dry run, and audit export to improve workflow.

nodes.label: Local LLM Integration
nodes.rationale: Local LLM support (LM Studio, Ollama) is a key differentiator but was documented yet untested; verification and auto-detection of localhost providers required before it can be claimed.

nodes.label: MCP Protocol Support
nodes.rationale: MCP enables ecosystem extensions (server/client protocol, stdio/HTTP/WebSocket transports, MCP tool adapter) but is medium priority since it is not critical for core functionality.

nodes.label: LSP Integration
nodes.rationale: LSP adds code intelligence (definitions, references, diagnostics via tower-lsp) but requires significant effort; classified nice-to-have at medium priority.

nodes.label: Plugin System (WASM)
nodes.rationale: WASM-based plugin runtime with sandboxing deferred to lowest priority: a major 7-10 day undertaking that benefits mostly power users and developers.

nodes.label: Quick Wins (High Value, Low Effort)
nodes.rationale: Five ~6-hour fixes prioritized for immediate impact: fix hard-coded model in render.rs, custom config path support, connection timeout, approval timeout, and a first database benchmark.

nodes.label: Plan Mode
nodes.rationale: Inspired by Claude Code's planning capabilities: the LLM explores the codebase read-only, produces a structured plan with subtasks, and executes only after explicit user approval. Goals: safer execution, better task management, user architectural control, progress tracking, and flexibility to use different models for planning vs execution.

nodes.label: Plan Mode Tool Restrictions
nodes.rationale: In Plan mode only read-only tools are allowed (read_file, ls, glob, grep, safe bash commands); write tools and mutating bash (redirects, pipes, git commit) are blocked by checking tool capabilities against the app mode in ToolExecutionContext, preventing uncontrolled modifications during exploration.

nodes.label: Priority Matrix
nodes.rationale: Quick-reference effort-vs-impact quadrant view of the roadmap: overall grade C+ (functional prototype, not production-ready); show-stoppers for 1.0 were single-provider support, crashes on network errors, plaintext API keys, untested local LLM, and a hard-coded model bug.

nodes.label: Project Rename: crusty to crustly
nodes.rationale: Full rebrand across folder, Cargo.toml, source (CrustyError to CrustlyError), env vars (CRUSTY_* to CRUSTLY_*), config paths, docs, and logo; one 'crusty' reference intentionally kept in README as a croissant pun.

nodes.label: Startup Splash Screen
nodes.rationale: Adds professional branding at launch (Rust crab ASCII art, version, model, provider); dismissed by any keypress with no timeout to respect the user's reading pace. Implemented as src/tui/splash.rs with a Splash variant added to AppMode.

nodes.label: Sprint 0: Project Setup and Initialization
nodes.rationale: Stub-first scaffolding approach: 30+ files across 17 module directories created before implementation, which the team noted worked well; SQLite conflict resolved by dropping rusqlite in favor of sqlx only.

nodes.label: Crabrace Integration (provider registry)
nodes.rationale: Provider registry successfully migrated from Catwalk to Crabrace; exposes fetch_providers(), health_check(), get_provider() via a local path dependency.

nodes.label: Error Handling System (CrustlyError + ErrorCode)
nodes.rationale: Custom error enum with 12 numeric error codes (ConfigNotFound=1000, ProviderAuthFailed=2001, etc.) using thiserror, for categorized, user-friendly errors from the start.

nodes.label: OpenAI Provider
nodes.rationale: 517-line implementation of the Provider trait supporting the official OpenAI API, custom endpoints, and local LLMs (LM Studio, Ollama) via OpenAIProvider::local(); includes SSE streaming, tool use, and per-model cost calculation.

nodes.label: Approval Timeout (auto-deny)
nodes.rationale: Approval requests auto-deny after 5 minutes so stale requests cannot leave the app in limbo; adds a color-coded visual countdown (green >3min, yellow 1-3min, red <1min) in the dialog.

nodes.label: Database Benchmark Suite (criterion)
nodes.rationale: First performance baselines: parameterized session/message create-get-list benchmarks (10-500 records) using criterion, enabling measurement before optimization.

nodes.label: Retry Logic with Exponential Backoff
nodes.rationale: src/llm/provider/retry.rs (426 lines): exponential backoff with jitter, selective retry distinguishing transient errors (network, 429, timeout, 5xx) from permanent ones (401, 400, 404) that fail fast; stream retry applies only to the initial connection since mid-stream retry is impossible.

nodes.label: Rate Limit Detection & Handling
nodes.rationale: Extracts Retry-After headers (which may be seconds or a date) from 429 responses, converts to ProviderError::RateLimitExceeded, and respects server-specified wait times with a fallback default.

nodes.label: Database Lock Recovery
nodes.rationale: src/db/retry.rs (365 lines): detects SQLite BUSY/LOCKED errors and retries with exponential backoff (5 attempts, 50ms-5s), plus busy_timeout=5000 on the connection string and 10s pool acquire_timeout for concurrent access.

nodes.label: Error Reporting Infrastructure (ErrorInfo)
nodes.rationale: Structured ErrorInfo with severity levels (Info/Warning/Error/Critical) and categories (Network, Database, Config, Input, Tool, Internal), color-coded display, and retry tracking (is_retryable, retry_count, next_retry) in src/tui/error.rs.

nodes.label: Database Layer (SQLite + SQLx)
nodes.rationale: Design decisions: Unix timestamps over ISO strings for simplicity and performance; foreign key cascades for automatic cleanup; archive (soft delete) instead of hard delete for sessions; connection pool capped at 5 for SQLite WAL mode; in-memory database support for fast tests.

nodes.label: Repository Pattern
nodes.rationale: Session, Message, and File repositories behind a common async Repository<T> trait provide clean separation between data access and business logic; prepared statements via SQLx give type-safe, injection-resistant queries.

nodes.label: Token & Cost Tracking
nodes.rationale: Message schema tracks input/output/reasoning/cache_creation/cache_read tokens and cost as optional fields to stay flexible across model types, including prompt caching support.

nodes.label: Service Layer (Session/Message/File services)
nodes.rationale: ServiceContext for shared resources plus ServiceManager for centralized access, with clean separation between services and repositories; includes automatic message sequence numbering and per-message usage statistics.

nodes.label: Model Type Alignment
nodes.rationale: Service and database layers disagreed on types (String vs Uuid ids, i64 vs DateTime<Utc>). Chose to modernize the database models rather than downgrade the services: custom FromRow implementations convert SQLite TEXT/INTEGER storage to Uuid/DateTime/PathBuf, with a migration to transform existing data.

nodes.label: Provider Abstraction Layer
nodes.rationale: A Provider trait (complete, stream, supports_streaming, supports_tools) with common LLMRequest/LLMResponse/ContentBlock types isolates the app from vendor APIs so Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, and Bedrock backends are interchangeable.

nodes.label: Agent Service
nodes.rationale: Orchestration layer between the UI and providers: manages conversation context, tool execution approval, response streaming, token usage tracking, and persisting messages to the database.

nodes.label: Tool Framework (Tool trait + ToolRegistry)
nodes.rationale: Async Tool trait (name, description, parameters, execute, requires_approval) with a HashMap-backed ToolRegistry; requires_approval on the trait is the hook the approval system builds on.

nodes.label: Terminal User Interface (Ratatui)
nodes.rationale: Ratatui-based ChatGPT/Claude-like terminal experience: four-panel layout (header, chat, input, status bar), mode-based navigation (Chat/SessionList/Help/Settings), and mpsc event channels so agent responses never block the UI.

nodes.label: Event-Driven TUI Architecture
nodes.rationale: All interactions flow through a TuiEvent enum and unbounded async channels; user messages spawn background tokio tasks so agent processing never blocks rendering, and rendering only happens on state changes or events.

nodes.label: Component Wiring (CLI to TUI)
nodes.rationale: Dependency-injection style assembly: CLI parses args, config loads with priority (defaults, system config, local config, env vars), database migrates on startup, AnthropicProvider + ToolRegistry (Read/Write/Bash) are injected into AgentService via builder pattern, then the TUI launches.

nodes.label: Sprint 8: Enhanced Testing
nodes.rationale: Grew tests from 139 to 182 (+31%) with CLI (24), streaming (10), and error scenario (9) suites; TUI component tests deferred because mocking a terminal backend is complex and manual testing already covers it.

nodes.label: Mock Providers (Streaming/Error/Working)
nodes.rationale: StreamingMockProvider, ErrorMockProvider, and WorkingMockProvider implement the Provider trait so tests need no API calls: fast (<3s total), deterministic, and able to simulate rate limits, timeouts, and malformed responses.

nodes.label: Markdown Rendering (pulldown-cmark)
nodes.rationale: src/tui/markdown.rs parses markdown to Ratatui widgets: headings, bordered code blocks with language labels, inline code highlighting, and horizontal rules integrated into chat message rendering.

nodes.label: Syntax Highlighting (syntect)
nodes.rationale: src/tui/highlight.rs uses syntect with lazy-loaded syntax sets (loaded once at startup to avoid per-render cost), supports 100+ languages with the Base16 Ocean Dark theme, line numbers, and graceful fallback for unknown languages.

nodes.label: Testing Summary
nodes.rationale: Canonical test inventory: 182 automated tests (130 unit + 9 integration + 24 CLI + 10 streaming + 9 error) plus a 9-scenario manual testing guide for real API validation; in-memory SQLite chosen for test speed and isolation.

nodes.label: Windows Build Fix Guide
nodes.rationale: The Rust GNU toolchain on Windows does not bundle MinGW tools (gcc, dlltool), so switching toolchains alone is insufficient; three fixes documented: MSYS2 MinGW-w64 install (recommended), standalone MinGW-w64, or WSL2 with MSVC.
